$comment: Machine-readable ABI contract for calling between Lux- and Fluxio-compiled code on the NUX VM. See docs/quill_fluxio.md (Phase 0.5) and docs/memory-map.md. This is the source of truth fluxlink (Phase B3) and any future compiler targeting this ABI validate against -- not just documentation to read and hope to match.

calling_convention.$comment: Verified empirically, not just asserted -- see src/test_abi_conformance.c.
calling_convention.argument_order: left-to-right push order: f(a, b) compiles to PUSH a; PUSH b; CALL f. A Forth `( a b -- )` word signature means the same thing (a pushed first/deeper, b pushed last/top) -- confirmed identical in src/test_abi_conformance.c's test_multi_arg_call_push_order (sub(10, 3) == 7, not -7).
calling_convention.call_mechanism: OP_CALL (opcode 0x24) to a fixed absolute address, 5-byte encoding (1 byte opcode + 4-byte big-endian immediate). See include/opcodes.h.
calling_convention.frame_locals: OP_FRAME (0x22) pops N values off the data stack into a dedicated locals[] region separate from the data stack; top-of-stack before FRAME becomes local 0 (src/vm.c ~line 526). OP_UNFRAME (0x23) restores the frame pointer WITHOUT touching the data stack -- a value pushed before UNFRAME survives as the return value.
calling_convention.return_value: Left on the data stack after OP_RET (0x25); the caller is responsible for consuming exactly the arity the callee's signature promises. No multi-value returns. Some Lux words are `( ... -- )` -- they push nothing back. A caller MUST know statically whether a given target pushes a value or not, since nothing at the call site distinguishes the two cases; Fluxio's `extern` declarations encode this explicitly ('extern void f(...)' vs 'extern int f(...)', src/fluxio_parser.c/fluxio_codegen.c, docs/quill_fluxio.md Phase B6/B7) -- calling a void target through the `int` form (or vice versa) desyncs the caller's stack accounting silently, not with a fault. See src/test_abi_conformance.c's test_fluxio_extern_void_end_to_end.
calling_convention.no_change_needed: Both luxc and fluxioc already emit this convention -- it's a property of the shared 55-opcode VM (include/opcodes.h), not something either compiler chose independently. Nothing to keep in sync beyond not breaking it.

linked_image_format.$comment: Corrected twice before any fluxlink code was written, both times by tests/analysis catching a design bug early rather than a working linker being patched after the fact. (1) Phase B1 smoke-testing (src/test_abi_conformance.c, test_dual_image_single_blob): the VM restricts PC execution to a SINGLE contiguous [image_base, image_end) window (src/vm.c: vm_create sets image_end = base_address + program_size; execution outside it faults 'execute outside program', src/vm.c ~line 266) -- a linked library can't be a second, independently-loaded VM image, so it's concatenated into the SAME blob as the app that links it. No VM or host-runner (cloister.c/nux.c) changes needed. (2) The trampoline table's SIZE cannot vary with the export count: the library is compiled once via `luxc -base` to expect its own code at one fixed address, so if the table directly preceded the code and grew on each new export, the code's address -- and every internal CALL/JMP baked into it at compile time -- would silently shift on every recompile. Fixed with a fixed-size reserved trampoline region (MM_ABI_TRAMPOLINE_RESERVE, include/memory_map.h) instead of one sized to the current export count.

layout.desc: ASCII 'NUX1' -- identifies this as a linked-library trampoline table, not arbitrary code.
Must exactly match the linking compiler's expected major version. Mismatch is a hard link error.
A linker may accept a library with a minor version >= its own (backward-compatible additions only).
Number of trampoline slots actually in use (<= the fixed capacity below).

One 5-byte JMP (opcode 0x21) per exported symbol, in the stable append-only order recorded in the library's committed *.symtab.json (see append_only_policy below), followed by OP_HALT-padded filler for any unused slots up to the fixed capacity. Slot order is the entire compatibility surface -- callers address symbols by slot index (baked in at compile time via `extern`), never by name at load time. Capacity: floor((MM_ABI_TRAMPOLINE_RESERVE - 12) / 5) = 816 slots with the current 0x1000 reserve.

layout.size: rest of the library's own compiled bytecode
layout.desc: Unmodified `luxc -base MM_ABI_LIBRARY_CODE_BASE` output -- MM_ABI_LIBRARY_CODE_BASE = MM_ABI_LIBRARY_LINK_BASE + MM_ABI_TRAMPOLINE_RESERVE is a fixed constant the library is always compiled against, independent of how many symbols it currently exports. Every trampoline JMP target points somewhere in here.

linked_image_format.base_address_band: MM_ABI_LIBRARY_LINK_BASE .. MM_ABI_LIBRARY_LINK_END (0x700000-0x800000), include/memory_map.h. Trampoline table occupies [MM_ABI_LIBRARY_LINK_BASE, MM_ABI_LIBRARY_CODE_BASE) = [0x700000, 0x701000); library code starts at MM_ABI_LIBRARY_CODE_BASE = 0x701000. A Lux library build targets the code base via `luxc -base 0x701000` (not the trampoline base).
linked_image_format.merge_procedure: fluxlink allocates one buffer spanning [app_base, MM_ABI_LIBRARY_CODE_BASE + lib_code_len), copies the app's own compiled bytes at offset 0, zero-fills the gap up to MM_ABI_LIBRARY_LINK_BASE, writes the header + trampoline table (padded to MM_ABI_TRAMPOLINE_RESERVE) at MM_ABI_LIBRARY_LINK_BASE, then the library's own code at MM_ABI_LIBRARY_CODE_BASE. That whole buffer is what gets loaded via the existing single-base-address vm_create()/machine_create() call path -- unchanged from how a standalone .bin loads today.

append_only_policy.$comment: The actual compatibility guarantee. See docs/quill_fluxio.md Phase 0.5 point 2.
append_only_policy.committed_symtab_file_pattern: lib/<name>.symtab.json, produced by `luxc -symbols` and checked into the repo
append_only_policy.rule: Once a library's symtab file is committed, an existing entry's index, name, and arity may never change. New exports may only be appended after the last existing entry.
append_only_policy.enforcement: fluxlink diffs a fresh compile's symbol table against the committed file and refuses to link (hard error, not a warning) on any reorder, rename, arity change, or removal of an existing entry.
append_only_policy.version_bump_policy: An incompatible change gets a new abi_version major number and a new base address band reserved in include/memory_map.h -- the old version's linked libraries keep working at their frozen addresses indefinitely. Never overwrite a shipped slot's meaning.

memory_bands.$comment: Mirrors include/memory_map.h exactly -- that header is the real source of truth for the VM/compilers; this block exists so a non-C tool (fluxlink's symtab tooling, docs generators) doesn't have to parse C to know the layout.

abi_library_trampoline_reserve.desc: Fixed-size trampoline table region; see linked_image_format above.

abi_library_code.desc: Where a linkable Lux library's own code is compiled to start (luxc -base 0x701000).

conformance_suite: src/test_abi_conformance.c -- any compiler targeting this ABI proves compliance by passing it, not by re-reading this document and hoping.
